A genuine gateway or provider 401 is still classified as auth (existing calibrated fixtures keep passing).

description:
The OMP auth absence pattern `401[^\n]{0,80}` (absence.CALIBRATED_AUTH_PATTERNS) matches any `401` in the text it scans, including pull request content echoed into the reviewer's output.

Observed 2026-10-23, both failing with omp exit code 1 because the tailnet policy did not open the gateway port:
- PR #3332, head ece15c335, oracle-verdict run 39953975498: the status read `large: absent (auth: 401 | `ORACLE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` does not match `client.token`. Run `secrets`. |\n+| Ga)`. The `+|` prefix in the captured detail shows it is a diff line from the PR's new troubleshooting table, not an HTTP response.
- PR #3331, run 39951571685: the same failure was recorded correctly as `error: exit code 1`.

An auth absence is treated differently from an error (auth absences are excluded from the same-reviewer retry), so diff text can change retry behavior and mislead diagnosis.
